report:
Reviewed the complete identity_before_detail claim, its sole implementation entry, and its complete sole annotated test, plus the captured review policy and the cited architectural-foundations identity section. Requirements are: identity exists before semantic details; it is retained independently of signature, members, fields, body and other lazy facts; symbol-bearing definitions use symbols; generic parameters, fields and locals use the appropriate scoped identity family; downstream values reference that identity instead of deriving it from detail. The cited rationale explicitly distinguishes top-level and associated symbol definitions, generic parameter identities, owner/index fields, and body-local IDs, so the claim does not require all identities to be erased Symbols.

The only implementation association is sage_meta::todo in service_spec.rs. Its explicit explanation defers uniform identity/detail isolation across every item kind and associated-item moves. This is an honest pipeline-wide implementation deferral covering the enumerated requirements; no ordinary implementation entry asserts completion. The one test, todo::crates_sage_ir_crate_identity_before_detail, is an empty TODO function. Its comment calls for identity/edit experiments demonstrating retained symbols under unrelated and detail-only changes and correctly keyed detail-query execution. It has no assertions and proves none of those properties. Test adequacy remains explicitly deferred, with uniform isolation across item families and associated-item moves, followed by substantive identity/edit experiments and their association/review, as prerequisites. Those future experiments must also exercise the scoped generic-parameter, field and local identities and downstream references, not just symbols. These are facets of the existing uniform-identity deferral, not completed coverage or a newly discovered behavior failure.

Accept the explicit TODO implementation and TODO test classifications; neither has been promoted to implemented or tested. There are no ordinary or N/A entries to assess and no helper calls in the associated test to follow. A downstream value reconstructed from a changed signature or a symbol changed by a body-only edit would violate the claim, and the current placeholder would not detect it; this is precisely why coverage stays TODO. Source inspection and review start/read/record commands constitute this review. No behavioral test command was run, and no runtime correctness or passing test evidence is claimed. No source edits are needed to preserve this honest deferral.
